title: Ines and the Bakery
premise: Casper Ashgrove, a marine biologist who fled to the coastal town of Saltmere after a betrayal he never talks about, is roped into the town library's anonymous pen-pal program meant to bridge old grudges. His letters land with Ines Marchetti, who has just inherited her late grandmother's failing bakery — and who blames Casper's family for the accident that broke hers twenty years ago. Neither knows who they're writing to, and through the letters they fall for the stranger while clashing in person as themselves. When the truth of both identities surfaces at the bakery's make-or-break harvest festival, Ines must choose between the loyalty she owes her family's memory and the truth of who Casper actually is; she lets him stay after the last train leaves, and together they reopen the bakery as something new.
about_author: Marguerite Dunmore is the pen name of a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes love stories set in small towns where ovens are always warm and grudges are always older than the people holding them. She lives by the sea with two opinionated cats and a sourdough starter named after her grandmother.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper counts turtle nests instead of answering his sister's calls, keeping his life in Saltmere small and safe. The library's anonymous pen-pal flyer catches him on a bad day, and on impulse he signs up. Beat: loneliness disguised as contentment, cracked open by one reckless decision.

chapters.title: Flour on Her Hands
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines returns to Saltmere to bury her grandmother and inherits Marchetti's Bakery along with its debts and its grudge against the Ashgrove name. She signs up for the pen-pal program hoping for an ally, not knowing the town's matchmaking librarian has other plans. Beat: grief braided with stubborn hope.

chapters.title: Dear Stranger
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. First letters cross: Casper writes about tides and turtles; Ines writes about bread and her grandmother's recipes. Both are disarmingly honest because they believe they'll never meet. Beat: the strange intimacy of telling a stranger everything.

chapters.title: The Man Who Bought the Wrong Loaf
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Casper walks into the reopened bakery out of habit and recognizes nothing, but Ines recognizes the Ashgrove jawline instantly. She serves him coldly; he leaves confused, having no idea why the baker hates him. Beat: first spark of friction, misread as simple dislike.

chapters.title: Tides Don't Apologize
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper vents to his pen pal about the hostile baker without naming her, and Ines vents right back about an arrogant scientist. Each defends the other's antagonist without realizing it. Beat: dramatic irony tightening like a knot.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept in the Tin
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Sorting her grandmother's things, Ines finds letters suggesting the Ashgrove accident wasn't what her mother always claimed. She hides the tin, unwilling to let facts disturb the loyalty that defines her. Beat: the first hairline crack in the family story.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm floods the bakery's cellar and damages Casper's research station; forced to shelter together, they argue, then work side by side until dawn. Something almost tender passes between them before Ines remembers herself. Beat: enemies discovering they fight well as a team.

chapters.title: Letters I Shouldn't Reread
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines realizes she's falling for her pen pal and feels guilty, as if betraying her family's memory by loving anyone warm. Meanwhile the bakery fails a health inspection and the bank calls. Beat: love arriving at the worst possible time.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Flashback chapter: the betrayal that drove Casper from his old life — a colleague stole his research and his engagement collapsed in the same season. He explains why he counts turtles: numbers don't leave. Beat: sympathy earned; the enemy becomes legible.

chapters.title: The Librarian's Little War
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The town librarian, delighted by her matchmaking, drops hints to each pen pal about the other's identity. Ines nearly learns the truth and panics, avoiding the post office. Beat: comedy masking dread; the secret grows heavier.

chapters.title: Bread for the Harbor Crew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Casper quietly orders bread for his whole research crew every week to keep the bakery afloat, anonymously. Ines discovers it and confronts him, certain it's charity laced with condescension. They fight properly this time. Beat: kindness mistaken for insult; pride on both sides.

chapters.title: The Tin, Opened
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines finally reads all the letters in her grandmother's tin and learns her grandmother had secretly forgiven the Ashgroves years ago — and had been exchanging recipes with Casper's late aunt. The feud was already over; only the children kept fighting it. Beat: grief and revelation colliding.

chapters.title: Almost Telling You
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both pen pals draft confessions and burn them. Casper decides to reveal himself at the harvest festival; Ines decides to ask her pen pal to meet there too. Neither knows they've chosen the same night. Beat: hope and dread running on parallel tracks.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The festival is the bakery's last chance. Casper shows up to help, and mid-crisis — a collapsed stall, a ruined batch — they move like partners. Ines catches herself laughing with him and hates how natural it feels. Beat: the wall thinning to paper.

chapters.title: The Letter Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the festival's closing bonfire, the librarian reads an anonymous letter aloud as tradition — and it's Casper's, unmistakably his. Ines goes white. In front of the whole town, she realizes her pen pal and her enemy are the same man. Beat: public unmasking; humiliation and heartbreak fused.

chapters.title: You Let Me Say Those Things
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines accuses Casper of manipulating her under cover of anonymity; he counters that she did exactly the same. Both retreat wounded. The bakery wins its festival order but Ines can't taste the victory. Beat: climax of anger; truth used as a weapon by both.

chapters.title: The Empty Platform
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Beaten down, Casper accepts a research post abroad and books the last train out of Saltmere. He leaves his final unsent letter with the librarian, addressed honestly: no pseudonym, just his name. Beat: surrender mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: Everything the Tin Couldn't Hold
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines rereads every letter with new eyes and sees what she refused to see: the man in them and the man at the counter were always one person, and she loved both. Her grandmother's forgiveness sits beside her own pride. Beat: the choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines runs to the station through rain and finds the platform empty, the tail lights gone. She stands in the dark believing she's too late — until Casper steps out of the waiting room; he missed the train on purpose, unable to leave without saying goodbye in person. Beat: despair flipping to grace.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is Not a Grave
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the empty platform they say the hard truths: her family's story, his exile, the years each spent guarding a wound. Ines tells him loyalty to the dead shouldn't mean imprisonment for the living. He asks to stay. She says yes. Beat: mutual confession; the feud formally ended.

chapters.title: First Batch, New Name
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Spring reopening: the bakery rechristened with both families' names above the door. Casper balances his research with early-morning shifts; the town pretends not to be smug. Ines bakes her grandmother's recipe with Casper's aunt's twist. Beat: found family assembled from broken pieces.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles, Counting Mornings
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Epilogue. One year later, Casper still writes letters — but now he slides them across the bakery counter to Ines, who answers out loud. The final image: two names in flour on the window, tide coming in, oven warm. Beat: safety chosen freely, not built from fear.
